subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
caption: B1 pupils exploring ideas for art from people and history in their local community.
altText: Lower primary pupils in Ghana looking at photos and drawings of elders, market women, farmers and local historical figures on a classroom wall.
detailedDescription: In a B1 classroom, a Ghanaian teacher has pinned photographs and simple drawings of important people from the local community: elders, market women, farmers, a nurse, a carpenter, a retired soldier and a local historian. Pupils stand in small groups, pointing and talking about who these people are, what they do and what makes them special. Some children hold sketchbooks where they quickly sketch faces, tools and clothing. The scene frames art as a way of honouring people, preserving stories and thinking deeply about local history instead of just copying patterns.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
caption: B1 pupils observing local buildings and artworks to collect ideas for drawing and painting.
altText: Ghanaian B1 pupils outside, sketching a mosque, a church, a colourful shop sign and decorated pots in their community.
detailedDescription: Outside the classroom, B1 pupils sit and stand near important buildings and objects from their local community: a simple mosque or church, a small kiosk with a hand-painted signboard, decorated clay pots and carved wooden stools. The teacher encourages them to look carefully at shapes, patterns and colours. Some children sketch doorways, windows and roofs; others draw patterns from the pots and signboards. The scene shows learners as visual researchers, collecting ideas from real places and artworks instead of only copying from textbooks.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
caption: B1 pupils using observation of the environment and topical issues as starting points for artworks.
altText: B1 pupils in Ghana observing a choked gutter, a clean compound and a road safety sign while discussing ideas for posters and drawings.
detailedDescription: Near the school, the teacher guides B1 learners to observe two contrasting scenes: a choked gutter with rubbish, and a clean swept compound with dustbins. A nearby road sign reminds people to cross carefully. The teacher asks learners what problems they see and how art can help. Some pupils sketch ideas for posters about keeping the environment clean or crossing roads safely. The scene trains children to connect creative arts with real problems in their community, seeing themselves as future solution designers, not spectators.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
caption: B1 pupils using idea journals and sketchbooks to record and organise visual ideas.
altText: Ghanaian B1 pupils seated at desks, drawing quick sketches and writing short notes in simple idea journals or sketchbooks.
detailedDescription: Inside the classroom, B1 pupils have simple sketchbooks or stapled idea journals. On each page, they draw quick sketches of people, buildings, objects and issues they have observed, and write short words or labels beside them. The teacher moves around, smiling and asking questions like ‘What do you want to say with this picture?’ or ‘Which of these ideas will you develop into a big artwork?’ The picture trains the habit of capturing and organising ideas, preparing children to think like designers, inventors and authors, not only performers of instructions.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Trying out different art media
altText: B1 pupils in a Ghanaian classroom experimenting with different art media like crayons, paint, collage papers and clay on a shared table.
detailedDescription: In a B1 classroom, small groups of pupils stand and sit around low tables covered with drawing papers. On the tables are crayons, coloured pencils, watercolours, scraps of coloured paper, glue and a little clay. Some learners test how crayons, pencils and paint make different lines and textures. Others press shapes in clay or tear and arrange coloured papers. The teacher moves around, asking what they notice and encouraging them to discover which media best fit the ideas in their minds.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Arranging ideas before making
altText: B1 pupils arranging cut-out shapes and small sketches on paper before gluing or drawing their final artwork.
detailedDescription: On the classroom floor and tables, B1 pupils place small cut-out pictures, shapes and quick pencil sketches on larger sheets of paper. They slide pieces around, discussing which arrangement tells their story best. Some work alone, others in pairs, pointing and arguing playfully as they decide where to position people, buildings, trees or symbols that show their community. The teacher stands nearby, reminding them to think about balance, space and what they want viewers to notice first.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Idea board for artworks
altText: A B1 class idea board covered with small sketches, colour tests and notes about artworks pupils want to create.
detailedDescription: At the front or side of the room, a large manila-sheet idea board hangs on the wall. It is filled with small sketches of market scenes, families, local games and important buildings, along with little colour-test patches and short written notes in simple English. Several B1 pupils stand in front of the board, pointing at sketches that match the artworks they are planning. The teacher guides them to connect their ideas on the board to media choices and compositions they will try in their sketchbooks or on larger paper.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: From sketch to finished artwork
altText: A B1 learner moving from simple doodles in a sketchbook to a more detailed, coloured artwork on a bigger paper.
detailedDescription: On a single desk, three stages of a B1 learner’s work are shown: a page of loose pencil doodles and scribbles where the pupil tried out different ideas, a clearer sketch showing the chosen scene, and a larger, coloured artwork on card or paper. The learner points proudly to the finished piece while the teacher or a classmate looks at both the sketchbook and final work. This scene highlights the idea that planning, experimenting and revising are part of making stronger, more thoughtful artworks.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Planning a simple classroom display
altText: B1 pupils and their teacher planning how to display drawings and paintings on a classroom wall.
detailedDescription: In a Basic 1 classroom in Ghana, a teacher and a small group of pupils stand in front of a bare wall. On a nearby table are several drawings and simple paintings about keeping the environment clean and caring for others. One child holds a sheet and points to a spot on the wall, another uses a ruler to measure space between pictures, while the teacher listens and guides them to decide where each artwork should go. The scene shows children thinking, suggesting ideas and planning a display together, instead of waiting for the teacher to do everything.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Arranging artworks to tell a story about a topical issue
altText: Basic 1 learners arranging their drawings in an order that tells a story about keeping the community clean.
detailedDescription: Several B1 pupils sit around a low table covered with drawings that show littering, sweeping, using bins and a clean neighbourhood. One child suggests which picture should come first, another moves a drawing to make the story clearer, while a third points to a simple plan sketched on a sheet of paper. The teacher stands back, asking guiding questions like, ‘Which picture should come before this?’ to help them think. The image emphasises decision making, storytelling and arranging artworks with purpose around a real community issue.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Classroom exhibition for peers and parents
altText: Basic 1 pupils presenting their displayed artworks about local issues to visiting peers and parents.
detailedDescription: A B1 classroom has been turned into a mini exhibition. Drawings and paintings about road safety, handwashing and caring for the environment are neatly displayed on the walls and hanging lines. A confident child stands beside their artwork, explaining its meaning to a small group of classmates and one or two parents. Another child listens and nods while holding a simple question card. The teacher observes proudly from the side. The scene positions children as young communicators and citizen-leaders using art to educate their community, not just as marchers in a parade.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Reflecting on the display and improving it
altText: Basic 1 learners gathered around their display, discussing what they like and what they would improve next time.
detailedDescription: After setting up a wall display of their artworks, B1 pupils sit in a semi-circle facing the display. One child points to a crowded section and suggests spacing the pictures more. Another comments that adding labels would help people understand the message better. The teacher writes some of their ideas on a small reflection chart headed ‘Next time we will…’. The atmosphere shows children thinking critically about their own work and learning to improve, building habits of reflection, ownership and continuous growth.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Observing visual artworks in the community
altText: Basic 1 learners on a short community walk observing signboards, murals, cloth patterns and carvings as examples of visual artworks.
detailedDescription: A Ghanaian Basic 1 class walks with their teacher through a nearby street or market. Children point at hand-painted signboards, colourful shop murals, patterned kente or wax prints hanging in front of a shop, and a carved stool or wooden figure. The teacher pauses at one or two artworks, asking children what they see and what it tells them about the people who live there. The scene shows learners noticing that visual artworks are already around them in everyday community spaces.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Bringing community artworks into the classroom
altText: Basic 1 pupils and their teacher creating a small classroom corner with photos and objects of visual artworks from the local community.
detailedDescription: Inside a Basic 1 classroom, there is a small ‘Community Art Corner’. On a board and table are photos or drawings of local signboards, kente patterns, pottery, baskets and carvings. Some children neatly arrange the pictures, others place a small basket or cloth sample on the table. The teacher helps them label the artworks with simple words like ‘basket’, ‘cloth’, ‘signboard’ and ‘stool’. The image presents the classroom as a thinking lab where community artworks are collected, honoured and used as inspiration.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Discussing meaning, history and culture in artworks
altText: Basic 1 learners sitting in a circle with their teacher, discussing what local visual artworks tell them about their history and way of life.
detailedDescription: B1 learners sit in a circle around a few enlarged pictures of local artworks: a festival poster, a carved stool, a cloth pattern and a painted wall. One child points to a picture while speaking, another listens with interest. The teacher prompts them with questions like ‘What do you think this shows about our people?’ and writes short key words on a chart. The image emphasises that children can think, interpret and talk about meaning in artworks, not just describe colours and shapes.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Planning own artworks from imagination
altText: Basic 1 pupils sketching simple ideas for artworks that reflect their community’s history and way of life.
detailedDescription: Back in the classroom, B1 learners sit in small groups with drawing paper and pencils. Each child sketches a simple idea for an artwork inspired by something they observed in the local community such as a market scene, festival, family gathering or local craft. On a wall chart the teacher has written prompts like ‘Who?’, ‘Where?’, ‘What are they doing?’. The teacher moves between groups, asking questions and encouraging children to use their imagination instead of copying exactly. The scene shows children planning meaningful artworks that speak about their own people and place.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Noticing visual ideas around us
altText: Basic 1 children in Ghana noticing colours, shapes, patterns and objects around the school as ideas for artworks.
detailedDescription: Outside a Ghanaian Basic 1 classroom, learners walk slowly with sketchboards or small notebooks. Some point to a bright bucket, patterned cloth on a line, a tree with interesting branches, and a painted signboard. The teacher encourages them to look closely and talk about colours, shapes and patterns they see. The picture shows that ideas for art come from paying attention to real life, not from copying one sample drawing on the board.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Creating an idea bank or sketchbook
altText: Basic 1 pupils drawing quick sketches and symbols into a simple personal sketchbook to store art ideas.
detailedDescription: In a B1 classroom, each child has a small ‘idea book’ or folded sketchbook. Learners quickly sketch simple symbols: a house, a mango tree, a water pot, a drum, a lorry, a football game. Some add short labels beside their drawings. The teacher moves around, smiling and encouraging them to keep any idea that comes to mind. The scene presents children as young designers building an idea bank instead of waiting passively for the teacher to tell them exactly what to draw.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Combining simple objects to form new ideas
altText: Basic 1 children using cut-out pictures or drawn shapes to combine everyday objects into new imaginative art ideas.
detailedDescription: At a low table, B1 learners play with cut-out pictures or simple drawn shapes: a drum, a tree, a house, a hill, a moon, people walking. In small groups, they arrange and rearrange the pieces to create new scenes such as a night festival on a hill or a family at the riverside. The teacher challenges them with questions like ‘What else can we add?’ and ‘What story does this show?’ The image trains children to combine simple elements to build fresh ideas, a core creative and entrepreneurial skill.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Sharing and choosing ideas to develop
altText: Basic 1 learners sharing their art ideas with classmates and choosing one idea each to develop into a full artwork.
detailedDescription: B1 children sit in a circle holding their idea books or sketches. One child stands to briefly show a favourite idea, while others listen and clap. On the board, the teacher writes simple criteria like ‘clear story’, ‘interesting’, ‘shows our community’. Each learner quietly chooses one idea from their sketchbook to develop in the next lesson. The scene shows learners practising communication, listening and decision making about their own creative work, like young project leaders choosing which project to execute.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Identifying topical issues in the community
altText: Basic 1 learners and their teacher observing choked gutters, refuse heaps and road safety issues in a Ghanaian community.
detailedDescription: On a short guided walk near the school, Basic 1 learners and their teacher observe real topical issues in a Ghanaian community. Some children look at a choked gutter with plastic waste, others notice a smoky refuse heap, a broken footpath or children crossing the road without a zebra crossing. The teacher calmly asks questions and notes ideas on a small card, helping the children see that problems in their environment can become subjects for visual artworks and solutions.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Looking at artworks that address topical issues
altText: Basic 1 pupils examining posters, murals and drawings that talk about cleanliness, flooding and road safety.
detailedDescription: Back in the classroom, Basic 1 learners gather around a display of simple posters, murals and drawings that show messages like ‘Keep our gutters clean’, ‘Do not burn rubbish here’, and ‘Use the zebra crossing’. Some images show flooded streets and clean streets for contrast. Children point at the pictures while the teacher prompts them to notice colours, symbols and words the artists used to talk about community problems and solutions.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Discussing how artworks reflect community issues
altText: Basic 1 children discussing how pictures of dirty gutters, clean streets and road signs show problems and solutions in their community.
detailedDescription: In a discussion circle, B1 learners sit with enlarged pictures of dirty gutters, clean streets, and clear road signs placed in the middle. One child points to an artwork of a flooded street and explains what might have caused it, while another points to a picture of a clean gutter and suggests what people did differently. The teacher writes key words like ‘problem’, ‘cause’, ‘solution’ on a chart. The scene shows children thinking beyond ‘nice picture’ into how visual art carries messages about real life issues.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Planning own posters about topical issues
altText: Basic 1 learners planning simple posters about keeping gutters clean, managing rubbish and staying safe on the road.
detailedDescription: Basic 1 children sit at tables with drawing paper, pencils and crayons, planning their own posters about issues like clean gutters, proper rubbish disposal and safe road crossing. On the board, the teacher lists guiding questions such as ‘What problem?’, ‘What do you want people to do?’, ‘What picture or symbol will show your message clearly?’. Learners sketch big symbols like crossed-out litter, clean gutters and people using a zebra crossing. The scene presents children as young citizens using art to speak into community problems.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Noticing art in the classroom and school
altText: Basic 1 learners in Ghana walking around their classroom and school, pointing to posters, drawings, patterns and decorations on walls and objects.
detailedDescription: In a Ghanaian Basic 1 school, the teacher leads learners on a short ‘art walk’ around the classroom and corridor. Children point at posters, alphabet charts with pictures, hand-made drawings, colourful borders, patterned curtains and painted doors. Some learners lean closer to look at details like colours, shapes and patterns. The teacher quietly prompts them to notice what looks beautiful, interesting or meaningful to them. The scene trains children to recognise that visual art is already all around them in their everyday school environment.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Talking about favourite artworks
altText: Basic 1 learners sitting in a small circle each holding or pointing to a classroom artwork they like, while sharing what they like about it.
detailedDescription: Inside the classroom, several artworks made by the pupils are arranged on the floor or low tables. B1 learners sit in a small circle, each child holding one drawing or pointing to a picture on the floor. One learner talks about why they like a particular artwork, mentioning colours, shapes, or the story it tells, while others listen. The teacher encourages them to use simple positive language like ‘I like... because...’. The scene develops children’s confidence to express personal preferences and feelings about artworks respectfully.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Asking and answering questions about artworks
altText: Basic 1 teacher and learners gathered around two or three artworks, taking turns to ask and answer simple questions about what they see and feel.
detailedDescription: A few pupil artworks are pinned on the board or placed on an easel. The teacher points to one picture and asks simple questions like ‘What do you see first?’, ‘How does this picture make you feel?’, or ‘What do you think is happening here?’. Different B1 learners take turns responding while classmates listen. Some learners also ask their own questions about the pictures. The scene shows children practising curiosity, observation and basic art criticism in a warm, non-threatening environment.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Choosing artworks for a simple class display
altText: Basic 1 learners and their teacher selecting a few artworks from many on the floor to display on the classroom wall.
detailedDescription: On the classroom floor, many drawings and paintings created by the children are spread out. A small group of B1 learners and their teacher crouch or kneel around them. The teacher reminds them of simple criteria such as ‘clear picture’, ‘strong message’ or ‘shows what we have been learning’. Learners point to and gently pick up selected artworks to place in a ‘yes’ pile for display. The scene teaches children to make basic aesthetic choices and to value quality, clarity and meaning in their visual communication.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Exploring colour, line, shape and size
altText: Basic 1 learners at tables exploring colours, lines, shapes and sizes using crayons, paints and simple cut-out shapes.
detailedDescription: In a Basic 1 classroom, learners sit in small groups around low tables. On each table are crayons, coloured pencils, simple paints and cut-out paper shapes. Some children draw thick and thin lines across their pages, others colour circles, squares and triangles in different sizes, while a few mix colours in shallow trays. The teacher walks around encouraging children to use words like ‘big’, ‘small’, ‘straight’, ‘curved’, ‘red’ and ‘blue’ as they explore. The focus is playful investigation of basic visual elements rather than copying a finished picture.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Creating simple patterns and arrangements
altText: Basic 1 learners arranging colours and shapes in repeating patterns on paper and on the floor.
detailedDescription: Several B1 learners sit and kneel on the floor with strips of paper, bottle tops, coloured cards and simple drawn shapes. They arrange these objects into repeating patterns such as red–blue–red–blue or circle–square–triangle–circle–square–triangle. Some children copy simple patterns shown by the teacher, while others invent their own sequences. The teacher highlights where the pattern repeats and encourages them to notice order and rhythm. The scene connects visual patterns in art to early mathematical thinking and design.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Using design elements to communicate ideas
altText: Basic 1 children designing simple posters or pictures using colours, shapes and sizes to make the main idea stand out.
detailedDescription: In the classroom, B1 learners work on simple posters or drawings about familiar topics such as ‘keep our classroom clean’ or ‘play safely’. Without showing any written slogans, the image focuses on how children use bright colours, big shapes and clear lines to draw the main message, for example a large dustbin, a sweeping brush, or children playing carefully. The teacher guides them to make important parts larger, clearer or brighter and to leave enough space around key images. The scene shows design elements being used deliberately to communicate meaning.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Reflecting on how design choices affect a picture
altText: Basic 1 learners comparing two similar drawings and talking about how colour, size and placement change the feeling and clarity of the picture.
detailedDescription: On the board or a large sheet, the teacher displays two simple drawings about the same idea, for example ‘keeping the school clean’. In one picture the main object is small, crowded and dull, while in the other it is larger, clearer and more colourful with better spacing. B1 learners sit close, pointing to differences and saying which picture is easier to understand or more attractive and why. The teacher helps them use simple words like ‘clear’, ‘bright’, ‘too many things’ and ‘easy to see’. The scene builds early habits of reflecting on design decisions and their impact.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Observing traditional arts in the community
altText: Basic 1 learners and their teacher on a short community walk, observing a carved stool, colourful cloth, a hand-painted signboard and a drummer.
detailedDescription: A Ghanaian Basic 1 class walks with their teacher through a nearby community space. They pause near a small square where they can see a carved wooden stool, colourful cloth hanging, a hand-painted signboard and a drummer practising on a traditional drum. Some children watch the drummer’s hands and movements, others point at patterns on the cloth and stool. The teacher gently asks questions to help them notice shapes, colours, sounds and movements. The scene introduces children to both visual and performing arts that belong to their own culture in a natural setting.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Comparing arts from past and present
altText: Basic 1 learners comparing pictures of older cultural items and more modern objects and performances on a classroom board or table.
detailedDescription: Inside the classroom, the teacher has arranged two groups of pictures on a board or table. On one side are older cultural items like traditional drums, clay pots and old-style houses; on the other side are modern objects such as a keyboard, plastic buckets and modern houses. B1 learners sit in pairs, pointing from one side to the other and quietly discussing what is similar and different. The teacher guides them to see that both past and present arts and objects have value and can inspire creative work.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Talking about meaning and values in arts
altText: Basic 1 learners sitting in a circle with pictures of festivals and performances in the centre, talking about what these arts mean for their community.
detailedDescription: B1 learners sit in a circle on the classroom floor around a few enlarged pictures: a festival dance, a choir singing, and people in special clothes for an important occasion. One child points to a picture while speaking, another listens carefully. The teacher prompts them with simple questions such as ‘When do people do this?’, ‘How do they feel?’, or ‘Why is this important to our people?’. The scene helps children link visual and performing arts to feelings, values and community identity.

subject: Basic 1 Creative Arts
figureLabel: Creating artworks and performances from culture
altText: Basic 1 learners in a classroom making drawings of cultural scenes while another small group practises a simple dance and drum performance.
detailedDescription: The classroom is set up like a small culture project studio. On one side, some B1 learners draw and colour scenes inspired by local life such as festivals, family gatherings or drummers and dancers. On another side, a small group practises a short performance using improvised drums on desks, hand claps and simple dance steps. The teacher moves between groups, guiding but not leading everything. The scene shows children using their own culture as a rich source for both visual artworks and short performances.
